question: A sector of a circle with radius 6 cm has a central angle of 60°. What is the area of the corresponding segment?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a segment = r² × [(πθ ÷ 360°) − (sinθ ÷ 2)]

⇒ Area = 6² × [(π × 60° ÷ 360°) − (sin60° ÷ 2)]

⇒ Area = 36 × [(π ÷ 6) − (√3 ÷ 4)]

⇒ Area = (6π − 9√3) sq. cm

**∴ The correct answer is (6π−9√3) sq. cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 60° O A B 6 cm 6 cm Segment 

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 6 cm

Central angle of the sector (θ) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

Area of sector = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × side²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of sector OAB = (60° ÷ 360°) × π × 6²

⇒ Area of sector OAB = (1 ÷ 6) × 36π = 6π sq. cm

⇒ Since two sides (OA and OB) are equal radii and the included angle is 60°, the remaining angles are also 60°. Thus, ▵OAB is an equilateral triangle with side 6 cm.

⇒ Area of triangle OAB = (√3 ÷ 4) × 6²

⇒ Area of triangle OAB = (√3 ÷ 4) × 36 = 9√3 sq. cm

⇒ Area of corresponding segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle

⇒ Area of corresponding segment = (6π − 9√3) sq. cm

**∴ The correct answer is (6π−9√3) sq. cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ is directly given by the formula A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc corresponding to a central angle θ can be calculated using the formula L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Area of Triangle in a Sector

The area of the triangle formed by two respective radii and their corresponding chord is obtained generally by A = (1 ÷ 2) × r² × sinθ.
